articles.title: An AI agent can be approved and still leave you with an unknown result
articles.excerpt: An approval answers whether an agent may attempt an action. It does not tell That distinction became concrete in a public discussion with Murthy G, the Agent Work Layer. The useful outcome was a chang…
articles.body: An approval answers whether an agent may attempt an action. It does not tell you whether a remote service completed it. That distinction became concrete in a public discussion with Murthy G, the developer of Agent Work Layer . AWL stages selected tool calls until a manager approves the work. I asked what happens when a service receives a call, but the gateway dies before it records the answer. The useful outcome was a change we could inspect and rerun. The uncertain interval Consider one approved operation: The gateway records that it is starting the operation. The receiver performs the effect. The receiver returns a result. The gateway records that result. A missing result after step 2 does not establish that nothing happened. Sending again may duplicate an effect.
articles.author: asagiman

articles.title: Voice Clone Technology: The Gap Between Capability and Consent
articles.excerpt: A few years ago, producing a convincing synthetic replica of a human voice required hours of studio-quality audio and specialized enterprise software. Today, it takes a few seconds of reference audio…
articles.body: A few years ago, producing a convincing synthetic replica of a human voice required hours of studio-quality audio and specialized enterprise software. Today, it takes a few seconds of reference audio and a web browser. The technical barrier to Voice Clone technology has virtually collapsed. But while the tech has become incredibly accessible, the ethical and legal frameworks surrounding it are still scrambling to catch up. To understand the current landscape, it helps to separate what voice cloning actually does from the broader category of text-to-speech. Standard text-to-speech asks a system to read text in a generic, recognizable voice. Voice Clone asks the system to read text as a specific person. The process works by extracting layers of vocal identity.

articles.body: 아마존 맥 할인에 이끌려 새 맥 미니를 샀다 — 그리고 내 약시 눈을 VR로 다시 깨우기까지 아마존이 새 맥 미니를 최대 149달러, 맥 스튜디오를 200달러 할인한다는 맥루머스 기사를 본 건 지난달 말이었다. 그때 내 책상 위에는 2018년형 맥북 프로가 팬을 돌리며 버티고 있었고, 오른손엔 수년째 쓰지 않던 안대 패치가 서랍 깊숙이 묻혀 있었다. 나는 약시(amblyopia) — 흔히 '게으른 눈(lazy eye)'이라 부르는 — 를 가진 개발자다. 왼쪽 눈이 오른쪽 눈보다 현저히 약하고, 뇌가 오른쪽 눈 신호만 우선적으로 받아들이면서 왼쪽 눈은 점점 더 '게을러'졌다. 기사를 읽고 바로 주문했다. 맥 미니 M2 프로, 32GB 램, 1TB SSD. 배송 알림이 뜨자마자 메타 퀘스트 3도 함께 주문했다. 새 맥으로 개발 환경을 새로 짜면서, 동시에 내 눈도 '업그레이드'할 수 있지 않을까 하는 막연한 기대 때문이었다. 첫날: 퀘스트를 쓰고, 마을에 들어섰다 퀘스트를 머리에 쓰고 컨트롤러를 잡자, 조용한 마을 광장이 펼쳐졌다. 하늘에서 동전 같은 것들이 날아오고, 붉은 가시들이 섞여 내려온다. 동전은 가보 패턴(Gabor pattern) — 방향성이 있는 부드러운 줄무늬 자극 — 이 입혀져 있었다. 시과학에서 대비 감도와 방향 선택성, 세밀한 디테일 처리를 유도하는 데 쓰는 바로 그 자극이다. "이게 다야?" 처음엔 그냥 리듬 게임처럼 느껴졌다. 동전을 때리고(펀치), 가시를 피하고(덕/회피). 하트가 세 개, 다 잃으면 재시작. 그런데 스테이지가 넘어가면서 무언가 달랐다.

articles.title: My DOCX converter learned that 'bold' is a negotiation, not a fact
articles.excerpt: I built a DOCX-to-Markdown converter thinking Word documents were simpler than PDFs. They're not. They're just lying in a different font. The first version used python-docx and trusted run.bold. Then…
articles.body: I built a DOCX-to-Markdown converter thinking Word documents were simpler than PDFs. They're not. They're just lying in a different font. The first version used python-docx and trusted run.bold . Then I fed it a contract drafted by a law firm. The entire document rendered as plain text. Turned out that document used character styles named "Strong" and "Emphasis" — visually bold and italic, but run.bold was None everywhere. Word doesn't have a single source of truth for formatting. It has at least four, and they fight. So I added a fallback chain: direct run properties → character style → paragraph style → the document's default styles → whatever LibreOffice would have done.

articles.title: How Un-Triaged Feedback Kills Developer Velocity (And How to Fix It)
articles.excerpt: Modern dev setups let us write and ship code faster than ever. But speed in your IDE doesn't matter if your incoming feedback stream is pure chaos. ​The biggest sink of developer hours isn't complex c…
articles.body: Modern dev setups let us write and ship code faster than ever. But speed in your IDE doesn't matter if your incoming feedback stream is pure chaos. ​The biggest sink of developer hours isn't complex code—it's un-coordinated feedback: Stakeholder A wants a section redesigned. Stakeholder B wants the opposite 2 hours later. ​You end up building, reverting, and rebuilding before the team even agrees internally. ​The Triage Rule ​Never let raw client or stakeholder notes flow directly into your dev queue or issue tracker. ​Always enforce a single triage step on your staging environment first: ​All visual notes stay pinned to staging. ​A designated lead reviews, groups, and resolves internal conflicts. ​Only officially approved rounds get pushed to dev/AI workflows.

articles.excerpt: Super Mario Sunshine was beloved at launch but grew to become one of the most divisive Mario games ever. Here's why it's worth playing in 2026.
articles.body: I can’t remember what I had for lunch yesterday, but I still remember the day Super Mario Sunshine launched in 2002. It was a summer's day and I couldn’t wait to line up at the GameStop in the Natick Mall to pick up my pre-ordered copy. It was getting rave reviews — a 9.4 from IGN, a 9.75 from Game Informer, perfect marks from Nintendo Power! — so it felt like an instant classic. articles.title: Analog astronauts: How living underwater can prepare humans for space missions
articles.excerpt: How living underwater can prepare humans for space missions
articles.body: I have been dreaming of doing research in space as an astronaut my whole life, but for some reason, the thought of working underwater made me nervous. I’ve known for a long time that astronauts train underwater to simulate different scenarios they’re likely to experience in space. Diving was never an issue for me, either — I even made it as far as becoming a certified rescue diver. So what was the problem? This summer, I led a simulated space mission in an underwater habitat called the Jules’ Undersea Lab. It is a research station that is located 22 feet (6.7 meters) underwater near Key Largo, Florida. You have to scuba dive to get in and out of the station. To become an aquanaut , you have to stay underwater for at least 24 hours in a so-called state of saturation.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 26, 2004: Cassini spacecraft takes 1st-ever closeup photos of Saturn moon Titan
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 26, 2004, NASA's Cassini spacecraft took the first close-up images of Saturn's largest moon Titan. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 26, 2004, NASA's Cassini spacecraft took the first close-up images of Saturn's largest moon Titan. The Cassini spacecraft would later drop off a probe on Titan named Huygens, which was a European spacecraft that hitched a ride to the Saturn system with the Cassini mission. But before Cassini dropped off its robotic passenger, it flew by Titan a few times and took some amazing photos . Cassini completed its first flyby on July 3, 2004, but when it swung by a second time on Oct. 26, it got about 300 times closer than it did the first time. At the closest point of this flyby, Cassini was 745 miles (1,200 kilometers) away from the surface of Titan. The spacecraft took hundreds of photos during this flyby , and these were the highest resolution views of Titan anyone had ever seen.
